title: Blood lead changes during pregnancy and postpartum with calcium supplementation.
ehr_evidence: Blood and urine samples were obtained monthly during pregnancy and the postpregnancy period for ≥ 6 months; environmental samples of 6-day duplicate diet, drinking water, house dust, gasoline, and ambient air were collected quarterly, with high-precision lead isotope ratios and lead concentrations obtained by thermal ionization mass spectrometry.
summary: A longitudinal prospective case series of 10 immigrant women to Australia (aged 19–32) provided with calcium carbonate or complex calcium supplements during pregnancy and 6 months postpartum, examining changes in blood lead concentration and lead isotopic ratios.
key_findings: Geometric mean blood lead at first sampling was 2.4 µg/dL (range, 1.4–6.5).
Hematocrit-corrected blood lead increased from a minimum during late pregnancy by 10 to 50% (geometric mean 25%).
During postpartum, blood lead increased by 30 to 95% (geometric mean 65%; n = 8) from the minimum value observed during late pregnancy.
Significant increases in lead isotopic ratios (206Pb:204Pb) from the late-pregnancy minimum occurred for 3 of 8 subjects (p < 0.01).
Extra lead flux released from bone during late pregnancy and postpartum ranged from 50 to 380 µg lead (geometric mean, 145 µg lead).
Geometric mean cord:maternal blood lead ratio was 0.72 (range 0.55–0.93) with r² = 0.93, confirming placental transfer of lead.
Calcium supplementation provided limited benefit for reducing lead mobilization during lactation, though it offered some protection during pregnancy by delaying lead mobilization.
captured_features: environmental lead (dustfall, drinking water, ambient air)
pathologies_diseases: lead exposure / lead toxicity (heavy metal mobilization)
study_design: Longitudinal prospective case series with non-conceiving controls
population: Female immigrants to Australia of child-bearing age (19–32 years) during pregnancy and 6 months postpartum
limitations: Very small sample size (10 pregnant subjects and 2 non-conceiving controls).
No placebo/control supplementation group due to feasibility and financial constraints.
Compliance relied largely on self-report checked by monthly tablet count.
Short follow-up with some subjects lost (e.g., subject 1231 returned to China).
